statement: There exists a predicate P on C={0,1} and A={0,1} such that (forall c in C)(exists A in A) P(c,A), but not (exists A in A)(forall c in C) P(c,A). Take P(c,A) iff A=c.
proof: For each c in {0,1}, choose A=c, proving the first statement. For the second, any fixed A in {0,1} fails P(c,A) at the other element c=1-A. Thus no A works for every c.

statement: Assuming MMW19 Theorem 1.2, for every oracle A and time-constructible s(n) >= n, search-MCSP^A[s(n)] has a one-pass algorithm using poly(s) space and update time, with Sigma_3 SAT^A queries of O~(s)-bit length. Therefore no lower bound can exclude every algorithm in an augmented streaming model permitting these transitions. By PH nesting, the same holds for Sigma_k SAT^A-oracle models for each fixed k >= 3.
proof: MMW19 Theorem 1.2 supplies, for every such A and s, a correct one-pass algorithm with O~(s) space, O~(s^2) update time, and Sigma_3 SAT^A queries of length O~(s). These bounds are polynomial in s, so the algorithm belongs to the augmented model. For fixed k >= 3, Sigma_3^A predicates are contained in Sigma_k^A by padding the quantifier prefix with dummy blocks. Thus an alleged lower bound excluding every algorithm in the augmented model contradicts this algorithm. This argument makes no claim for k < 3 or for stricter resource or query-length bounds.

statement: Assume the exact hypotheses and conclusion of MMW19 Theorem 1.2. For every fixed k≥3, an augmented one-pass streaming model that permits Σ_k^A-SAT oracle queries of length at least the theorem’s O~(s(n)) bound, and allows at least its O~(s(n)^2) update time and O~(s(n)) space, cannot have a lower bound excluding all algorithms for search-MCSP^A[s(n)].
proof: Fix any oracle A and any time-constructible s(n)≥n covered by Theorem 1.2. That theorem supplies a correct one-pass search-MCSP^A[s(n)] algorithm using a Σ_3 SAT^A oracle, O~(s(n)) query length, O~(s(n)^2) update time, and O~(s(n)) space. For fixed k≥3, Σ_3^A predicates are expressible in Σ_k^A by adding dummy quantifier blocks, so the same algorithm is allowed in the stated augmented model. Its resource bounds meet that model’s allowances. Therefore a lower bound excluding every algorithm in that model would exclude this algorithm, contradicting the theorem. This implication is conditional on the cited theorem and says nothing about k<3 or models with tighter query or resource limits.

statement: Let k≥0 be fixed. Suppose R(c,x) is a uniformly specified predicate in Σ_k^P, with c and x given as inputs and one polynomial bound applying to all inputs. Define A* = {⟨c,x⟩ : R(c,x)} and A_c = {x : R(c,x)}. Then A*∈Σ_k^P and A_c={x:⟨c,x⟩∈A*} for every c.
proof: By definition, membership in A* is decided by the same Σ_k^P predicate R on input ⟨c,x⟩, so A*∈Σ_k^P under the stated uniform polynomial bound. For each fixed c, the section of A* obtained by fixing the first coordinate to c is exactly {x:R(c,x)}=A_c. The encoding map x↦⟨c,x⟩ is polynomial-time for each fixed c. Hence the family is represented by one oracle, with each member recovered by tagged queries. This statement concerns oracle membership and does not assert that any separate lower-bound property P(c,A_c) transfers to P(c,A*).

lemma: LEMMA (tagged-oracle simulation with query-cost bound). Let C be a finite set with an injective encoding enc_C of length b bits. Let R(c,x) define A_c={x:R(c,x)} and A*={(enc_C(c),x):R(c,x)}. Any deterministic algorithm making q queries to A_c, each of length at most L, can be simulated with A* using exactly q queries of length at most b+L+O(1), by replacing each x-query with (enc_C(c),x). The simulation preserves the answer sequence, internal transitions, and output. Proof: For each query x, the definition of A* gives A*((enc_C(c),x))=1 iff R(c,x), iff A_c(x)=1. Thus each answer agrees. Induction over the query sequence gives identical configurations and output. The tag and fixed delimiter/length encoding add b+O(1) bits. This makes no claim about the cost of computing R or enc_C, nor about transfer of a lower-bound property.

statement_start: LEMMA (ORACLE-LOCALITY Barrier for search-MCSP^A streaming). Assume MMW19 Theorem 1.2 holds as stated: for every oracle A and time-constructible s(n) >= n, search-MCSP^A[s(n)] has a one-pass streaming algorithm using O~(s(n)) space, O~(s(n)^2) update time, and Sigma_3 SAT^A oracle queries of length O~(s(n)). For any fixed k >= 3, consider an augmented one-pass streaming model that permits Sigma_k^A-SAT oracle queries of length at least the theorem's O~(s(n)) bound, and allows at least its O~(s(n)^2) update time and O~(s(n)) space. Then no lower bound can exclude all algorithms in this augmented model for search-MCSP^A[s(n)]. Any lower bound claiming to do so would contradict the existence of the MMW19 algorithm, hence would prove a false statement. Therefore, any valid lower bound for search-MCSP^A[s(n)] streaming must either (a) target k < 3, or (b) exploit a resource bound tighter than the MMW19 theorem's allowances (e.g., query length o(s), update time o(s^2), space o(s)).
statement_end: Therefore, any valid lower bound for search-MCSP^A[s(n)] streaming must either (a) target k < 3, or (b) exploit a resource bound tighter than the MMW19 theorem's allowances (e.g., query length o(s), update time o(s^2), space o(s)).

statement_start: PROOF of ORACLE-LOCALITY Barrier (S0005). Fix any oracle A and any time-constructible s(n) >= n covered by MMW19 Theorem 1.2. The theorem provides a correct one-pass search-MCSP^A[s(n)] algorithm using a Sigma_3 SAT^A oracle, O~(s(n)) query length, O~(s(n)^2) update time, and O~(s(n)) space. For any fixed k >= 3, the Sigma_3^A predicate is expressible in Sigma_k^A by adding dummy quantifier blocks (universal then existential pairs that don't change the truth value). Thus the MMW19 algorithm's Sigma_3^A oracle queries are valid Sigma_k^A oracle queries in the augmented model. Its resource bounds (query length, update time, space) are exactly within the augmented model's allowances. Hence the MMW19 algorithm is a valid algorithm in the augmented model. Any lower bound excluding ALL algorithms in this augmented model would exclude the MMW19 algorithm, contradicting the correctness of MMW19 Theorem 1.2. The argument is conditional on MMW19 Theorem 1.2 holding as stated. It identifies the exact escape hatches: k < 3, or resource bounds strictly tighter than O~(s), O~(s^2), O~(s).
statement_end: It identifies the exact escape hatches: k < 3, or resource bounds strictly tighter than O~(s), O~(s^2), O~(s).

statement_start: LEMMA (NATURAL-PROOFS Barrier for search-MCSP^A streaming). Assume the standard cryptographic assumption: there exists a pseudorandom generator G: {0,1}^r -> {0,1}^n with seed length r = n^o(1) secure against n^omega(1)-size circuits. Consider any lower-bound argument for search-MCSP^A[s(n)] streaming that proceeds by exhibiting a property P of Boolean functions on n bits that is (1) constructive: P is decidable in poly(2^n) time given the truth table (or in poly-resource time given the algorithm description in the streaming model), (2) large: P holds for at least a 1/poly(2^n) fraction of all 2^{2^n} Boolean functions on n bits, and (3) useful: every Boolean function computable by the target streaming model (with its resource bounds) satisfies P. Then such a property P would break the PRG (by the Razborov-Rudich natural proofs argument), contradicting the cryptographic assumption. Therefore, under this assumption, any valid lower bound for search-MCSP^A[s(n)] streaming must violate at least one of constructiveness, largeness, or usefulness-as-a-property-of-the-function-alone.
statement_end: Therefore, under this assumption, any valid lower bound for search-MCSP^A[s(n)] streaming must violate at least one of constructiveness, largeness, or usefulness-as-a-property-of-the-function-alone.

statement_start: PROOF of NATURAL-PROOFS Barrier (S0007). By the Razborov-Rudich natural proofs theorem (JACM 1997), if there exists a PRG G: {0,1}^r -> {0,1}^n with seed length r = n^o(1) secure against n^omega(1)-size circuits, then any property P of n-bit Boolean functions that is (i) constructive (decidable in 2^O(n) time given the truth table), (ii) large (holds for at least a 2^{-O(n)} fraction of all functions), and (iii) useful against a circuit class C (every function in C satisfies P), cannot exist. The search-MCSP^A[s(n)] streaming model computes some class C_stream of Boolean functions. If a lower bound argument exhibits a property P satisfying (1)-(3) for C_stream, then P is a natural property useful against C_stream. By Razborov-Rudich, this breaks the PRG, contradicting the assumption. Hence no such property P can exist. Any valid lower bound must therefore use a property that is either non-constructive (not decidable in poly(2^n) time), non-large (holds for less than 1/poly(2^n) fraction of functions), or not useful as a property of the function alone (i.e., usefulness depends on the algorithm's internal structure, not just the computed function). The argument is conditional on the standard PRG assumption.
statement_end: The argument is conditional on the standard PRG assumption.
